Evaluation infrastructure and historical build evidence

Archived detailed status as of 9 October 2026; comparative evaluations remain deferred. For public product readiness, use What works today.

This is a requirement-level status check against the build charter, updated 9 October 2026. Product positioning is existing-tool analytics. Rystic provides the initial comparative test environment.

Requirement Current evidence Status and limit
Bring existing-tool data into DuckDB Generic imports and snapshot tests; export recipe; 101-entry catalog, bundled templates, repaired adapters, readiness checks and source configure/sync/bootstrap/refresh CLI Local file lifecycle, controlled adapter contracts, actual SQLite dlt extraction and selected loopback REST/GraphQL extraction are verified through query, refresh and context preservation. API partial failures preserve prior snapshots. Vendor compatibility remains unverified. See connector guide.
Analyze, transform and make reviewed local changes Export recipe exercises mismatched IDs, blocked ambiguous mappings, exact-preview changes and a materialized result Working. Source systems and input export files remain unchanged.
Bootstrap and review context Schema/key/join observations, explicit authored rules, witnessed proposal, exact-hash approval and archived versions Working as draft generation and operator review. Autonomous business-definition discovery is not demonstrated.
Reuse outside the first session Functional receipt records two separate consumer processes executing exported definitions on freshly imported data Programmatic portability verified. A second LLM selecting the right definition on unseen questions remains to be measured.
Correct refresh using the same definition Generic fixture changes from 51 unused seats/five organizations to 8/one; Rystic functional run changes five accounts/$1,857.69 to four/$1,490.61 Verified functional outcomes. Generic replacement is explicit per table; materialized transforms do not auto-refresh.
Real Rystic use Native simulator receipts, versioned API seeding, paginated reads and source-change checks Original fixture verified on native Stripe 0.0.8/Linear 0.0.1. New shuffled-case variant is tested locally but awaits a live integration run.
Fair common agent comparison Warm and observed-phase pilots share one agent loop, actual stdio MCP, identical result calculator and policy-only context, exact recipe SQL, native source schema examples, timed source-session verification and independent scoring Runner and all four phase types verified with authored responses/source doubles; no Rystic comparative model result yet. Prior result hashes are excluded equally; fresh retrieval still requires trace review.
Held-out preparation Reproducible allocation, shuffled cases and paired order; twelve semantic templates; distinct acceptance intent/protocol/binding commands verify allocated baselines, substantive review inputs and later source evidence Offline contracts pass synthetic tests, including all phases with actual local DuckDB. Actual isolated native provisioning, power/accounting/rate reviews and an approved execution budget remain necessary. Existing development artifacts remain ineligible.
Budgeted study execution Controller enforces cumulative budgets, frozen source assignments/context and phase order; retains partial failed runs and disables automatic resume Implemented and tested end to end with in-memory sources and scripted responses. Native lifecycle, provisioning and authorization integration remain unverified; no native controller run or comparative model result is claimed.
Refresh and appropriate abstention Independent phase gold, complete validation/refusal receipts, durable refresh attempts and identical MCP status; an exact-approved transition executor checks full before/after state and retains uncertain or partial writes Source doubles and actual local MCP verify refusal/recovery offline. Native metadata transitions and the new validation path still need Rystic integration checks. The transition executor does not import a workspace. Intent hashes are not observed source hashes.
Full costs, failures and confidence intervals Acceptance reporting rescores common-engine receipts, checks full order/verification and includes recorded review/transition/refresh events in paired comparisons; private receipts and controller ledgers retain paid failures Synthetic controller and report tests pass. Actual native measurements, reviewed billing rates and complete billing reconciliation remain missing. Initial offline validation/construction and final reporting/export fall outside the measured runtime interval. Development or warm-only reports cannot satisfy the recurring benchmark contract.
More accurate, cheaper and faster No qualifying completed acceptance study Unverified. All three targets and confidence requirements remain unchanged.
Registry import/update round trip Portable bundles, separate create/append bodies and explicit target mapping; the native structural validator accepted six exported definitions and rejected an unsupported-spec control (receipt) Export/reuse and local semantic revision work. The native CLI does not execute SQL or validate full endpoint admission. Real Registry create/read/append, remote identity, versioning and access remain unverified.
Own-tool activation and retention GTM learning gates and observation plan No design-partner trials, repeat-use or commercial-conversion evidence has been collected.

Next sequence

  1. Review connector-specific dependencies and verify selected vendor authentication with explicitly authorized source access. Native SQLite and selected loopback REST/GraphQL checks have passed; keep their evidence separate from authenticated vendor use.
  2. Measure a new user's configure → sync → bootstrap → query → refresh experience on their own tools, including credential setup, source permissions and required business-definition review.
  3. Validate approved own-tool use with design partners and a real Registry consumer/update round trip. No source data or artifacts are published automatically.
  4. Resume comparative evaluations only when requested. The existing Rystic pilot and held-out study contracts remain deferred; their evidence and accounting requirements still apply before performance claims.

The core can be tried without Rystic or an Atlan account. The live comparative phase requires an available Rystic runtime and an explicitly bounded model run. Offline tests and pre-registration artifacts do not substitute for that measurement.

The controller's measured runtime starts after offline protocol/input validation and runtime construction, and stops before final statistical reporting and export. This analysis overhead is excluded and unmeasured; it is not a measured zero. Complete billing reconciliation, including an explicit treatment of these exclusions, remains required before any all-in claim. The controller and standalone acceptance-report replay enforce this by retaining charter_ready: false for unreconciled runs while preserving their separate statistical results.

The sequential collection design records the required order, provisioning boundary, remaining acceptance contracts and accounting decisions.
